newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem defends Argentine transport, fuel price hikes.
newsitem.headline: Menem defends Argentine transport, fuel price hikes.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem defended increases in bus fares and fuel prices that took effect on Tuesday under Economy Minister Roque Fernandez's fiscal austerity package, approved by Congress last week.

Menem, who faced a general strike last week in protest at new taxes and his proposed new labor laws, told local radio that the country could not afford "to maintain unrealistic prices, a situation which has stopped transport firms renewing their fleets."
The lowest bus fare in Buenos Aires rose to 0.55 pesos from 0.50 and longer-distance fares rose by up to 17 percent.
Pump prices for diesel rose to about 0.43 pesos per liter from 0.30, for high-grade gasoline to 0.95-1.0 pesos from 0.84-0.89, and for low-grade gasoline to 0.77 pesos from 0.66.

Fernandez's tax package, aimed at narrowing the budget deficit this year and next year, included a 46 percent hike in the tax on diesel fuel, a 12 percent increase in the tax on gasoline, and a 10 percent hike in the tax on new diesel cars.
Congress has also passed a new law letting the central government keep all the revenue from the fuel tax hikes rather than sharing it with the provinces.
Service stations were doing thin trade on Tuesday. Drivers apparently filled their tanks yesterday to beat the price increases that came into effect at midnight last night.
Train and subway fares are to rise by up to 15 percent in 10 days.
